correctedState: Confirmed gap, with narrower exposure than 'every agent write' suggests. Nessy has no `modified` frontmatter stamp anywhere in the memory subsystem: both writers -- the agent-facing `remember` tool (packages/session-tools-core/src/handlers/remember.ts:27-36, registered at tool-defs.ts:981) and the UI/RPC path appendMemoryFile (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts, called from packages/server-core/src/handlers/rpc/sessions.ts) -- append a plain bullet and never parse or rewrite a `---` block, and `grep -ran modified` over packages/shared/src/agent/memory/ and packages/session-tools-core/src/ returns zero hits. The scheduled rewrite pass (memory-cleanup.ts) is equally frontmatter-blind. Exposure is limited to hand-authored frontmatter, since Nessy's writers seed files as `# Memory` + bullets and never add frontmatter themselves. Nessy does record a per-entry write DATE -- the `<!-- nessy:auto:YYYY-MM-DD -->` marker (remember.ts:21-25, AUTO_MEMORY_MARKER_REGEX_SOURCE in memory-store.ts) -- but it is day-granular, per-entry rather than per-file, and stripAutoMemoryMarkers removes it in mergeMemoryContents before the prompt is built, so unlike Claude's `modified` it gives the model NO freshness signal; it exists solely so memory-cleanup can tell agent-written lines from human ones. The one frontmatter parser in the package, parseRuleFile (memory-store.ts:212-256), belongs to the sibling .agents/rules path-scoped-rules subsystem, is read-only, and understands only path/paths/glob/globs. Upstream gates the field on Claude Code v2.1.214+.
